title: Stitch sidecar proto pad
content:
One-line summary:
A small, deployable sidecar that composes multiple compatible model variants at inference time (stitching different specialists / quantized variants) to optimize cost and latency while preserving user-level quality constraints. This is a personal sketch for an exploratory prototype - lightweight, low-risk, incremental on top of existing serving runtime hooks.

Motivation / problem:
- Customers want to combine cheaper quantized or distilled submodels with expensive higher-fidelity models to reduce cost while avoiding quality regressions on critical requests.
- Current multi-model routing is coarse (route per-request to one model). Fine-grained per-token/model stitching is powerful but risky and heavy to implement in the main runtime.
- Need an intermediate approach that is: easy to deploy (sidecar), model-agnostic, supports per-tenant policies, and integrates with caching/batching.

Goals:
- Prototype a sidecar that can: 1) decide per-request whether to attempt a cheap model pass; 2) conditionally call a higher-fidelity model for targeted spans (e.g., completion fail / low-confidence tokens); 3) merge outputs preserving token alignment and provenance.
- Expose simple policy language for fallbacks and quality checks (confidence thresholds, shard-level heuristics).
- Keep changes outside core runtime to reduce blast radius and accelerate iteration.

Non-goals (for prototype):
- Full token-level attention merging or distributed KV-transfer between models.
- Complex retraining or model surgery.
- Enterprise multi-region HA or billing plumbing (we'll emit events for billing).

Persona(s):
- Small SaaS product that needs to limit inference cost but cannot tolerate hallucinations on product-critical snippets (e.g., legal text generation).
- Internal platform team wanting a knob to A/B cheap vs precise outputs per-customer.

High-level design:
- Deployed as a sidecar next to the existing model endpoint. Calls into Redwood runtime via a stable local API or gRPC, using the same request envelope.
- Flow: request -> sidecar preprocessor -> cheap-model call (optional) -> quality-checker -> if pass: return merged response; else: call expensive fallback model -> stitch / choose final output -> return.
- Quality checker: lightweight heuristics + optional small classifier model for failure detection. Emits a score and reasons.
- Stitching: for prototype, use a simple replace-at-span strategy (e.g., if cheap-model returns tokens t0..tn and classifier says low-confidence on tokens i..j, request expensive model for suffix starting at token i-1 and concatenate). Keep provenance metadata in response headers.

User stories:
- As an app engineer, I can opt my route into the sidecar and set a cost-vs-quality policy per-tenant (e.g., max 40% cheap-model usage).
- As an SRE, I can view metrics: percent cheap-pass, avg latency delta, fallback rate, token-level confidence histogram.
- As a product manager, I can run canary test where 10% of requests use the sidecar and compare cost & accuracy against baseline.

API sketch (local):
- POST /sidecar/v1/infer  (body same as Redwood runtime request envelope).
- Query params / headers: X-Policy-Id, X-Enable-Provenance.
- Response: { text: string, provenance: optional string[], policy: id, path: ["cheap-pass" | "fallback"], metrics: {confidence: float} }  (we'll return provenance as encoded header to avoid big payloads).

Policy primitives (small DSL idea):
- max_cost_delta: numeric (max extra tokens/calls allowed per request budget)
- confidence_threshold: float (0..1) for cheap model pass
- fallback_mode: [suffix-retry | full-retry | hybrid-stitch]
- sample_rate: float (for experimentation)
- allow_cache_eviction: boolean

Telemetry / observability:
- Emit events: cheap_attempt (ok|low_confidence), fallback_invoked, stitch_completed, fallback_latency_ms, cheap_latency_ms, token_count_cheap, token_count_fallback.
- Sampled traces linked to request ids so Console can show per-request model path and cost breakdown.
- Tag events by policy_id, tenant_id, route.

Safety / quality concerns:
- Stitching risks: misaligned tokenization between models, non-deterministic token boundaries, and context length differences. For proto: only stitch on suffixes (fallback from N-1 token).
- Metric leak: sidecar observes higher-level content. Ensure we follow privacy boundary rules; sidecar runs in same tenant boundary.

Prototype milestones (2-3 sprint plan):
- Sprint 1: Minimal local sidecar that proxies request to cheap model and returns cheap output with basic confidence heuristic. Emit telemetry.
- Sprint 2: Add fallback flow with suffix-retry stitching and provenance header. Implement policy config (simple JSON).
- Sprint 3: Dashboard in Console (basic charts), canary rollout, collect qualitative failure cases and refine heuristics.

Compatibility notes / integration points:
- Use existing runtime local adapter interface (TODO: confirm adapter API shape).
- Reuse tokenization utilities from runtime to avoid token mismatch. If not possible, restrict prototype to same tokenizer models.
- Integrate with Optimize for recommending policy presets (after data collected).

Open questions / risks:
- How to compute cheap-model confidence cheaply and reliably? Heuristic vs small classifier tradeoff.
- Accounting: how to attribute tokens to models for billing in combined responses? Emit detailed events; billing system needs to evolve.
- Edge cases: when cheap-model hallucination is persuasive and extends long - suffix-retry might not fix. Need metric-driven stop conditions.

Experiment ideas / evals:
- Run synthetic workload with known gold labels to measure precision/recall of cheap-pass + fallback versus always-expensive baseline.
- A/B live traffic: track cost per 1k requests, fallback rate, human-rated quality delta on sampled corpus.

Next steps (actionable):
- Sync with runtime owners to confirm local adapter API and tokenizer reuse (invite: @Noah Garcia).
- Spike confidence classifier (binary) on 5k examples from existing evals.
- Draft a minimal policy JSON schema and proto sidecar server that wraps existing model endpoints.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Keep prototype plumbed as opt-in flag on route to avoid accidental rollout.
- Save examples where stitching helped + where it made things worse (we will need a small "regression set").
- Reach out to Console team about adding a tiny path visualization for per-request trace.

Rough timeline: 6 weeks to first canary if prioritized (1 dev + 0.5 SRE + small runtime review).

End of sketch.
